clue.text: No other movie leaves one cracking up and delighted

indicators.note: leaves says a letter is left out of the pool of letters before it is rearranged
cracking up suggests the words breaking apart and being put back together in a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A film so unlike any other that it leaves the audience in fits of laughter and thrilled.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of NO OTHER MOVIE, let 'one' (I) 'leave', and the remaining letters, 'cracking up', rearrange to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being over the moon is an idiom for being extremely happy and pleased.

clue.text: Hope the majority of time in work isn't so manic initially

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a musical work

indicators.note: the majority of a word is all but its last letter, so one letter is dropped
initially says take the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Someone hopes most of their working hours will be less frantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The majority of' drops the last letter of 'time'; 'in' is only a link here, since the pieces sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimism is hopefulness, a confident expectation that things will turn out well.

clue.text: Damn, this is what a senior manager charges?!

parts.note: an exec is an executive, a senior manager
a rate is what someone charges for work

explanation.surface: An outraged cry at the fees a top manager bills for their time.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation 'Damn' is the definition, in its verb sense of condemning; the rest reads as a pun on an executive's rate.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to curse or denounce bitterly, the same as to damn someone.

clue.text: One way you could begin to characterise 'aggressive'?

definitions.text: One way you could begin to characterise 'aggressive'?

parts.words: One way you could begin to characterise 'aggressive'?
parts.note: a pushy, competitive person is described with a personality label; read literally, keying the word aggressive starts with one particular key press

explanation.walkthrough: Two readings meet: a Type A personality is the hard-driving, aggressive kind, and to start writing the word 'aggressive' on a keyboard you would type 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Type A is the psychological label for a competitive, impatient, aggressive personality.

clue.text: Passes English, with minor mistakes?

parts.note: lapses are small slips or errors

explanation.surface: A student gets through an English exam despite a few small errors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passes' looks like an exam result, but here it means time going by.
explanation.definitionFit: When time elapses it passes or slips away.

clue.text: Without exception, skill is seen in a certain hospital

indicators.note: is seen in places one piece inside the others

parts.note: one, as in 'one day', means a certain
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
art means skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: Remarkable talent shows up at one particular hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without exception' fits the intensifying use, as in 'nothing on earth could stop him'.
explanation.definitionFit: On earth is an intensifier, as in 'no reason on earth', meaning at all, with nothing excepted.

clue.text: Bothersome individuals — ones going into the finer details

indicators.note: going into says one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: nuances are subtle distinctions or fine details
ones written as Roman numerals gives I's

explanation.surface: Annoying people are the ones who dig into every little detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ones' is read as the plural of the Roman numeral I, an apostrophe-free plural.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuisance is an annoying person, so nuisances are irritating individuals.

clue.text: Very variable, casual apology

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
Z is a letter used for a variable in algebra

explanation.surface: Someone with very changeable moods offers a flippant 'sorry'.
explanation.definitionFit: Soz is slang for sorry, a throwaway way of apologising.

clue.text: Bald-faced liars finally take note

indicators.note: finally says to use the end letter of the word before it

parts.note: to have something is to take it, as in have a biscuit

explanation.surface: Brazen liars eventually get noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bald-faced' reads as brazen, as in a bald-faced lie, but here means a face without hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaven face has had its beard removed, leaving it bare of hair.

clue.text: Online chat with journalist went by quickly

parts.note: Zoom is the video-call service used for online meetings
ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A video call with a reporter that flew past.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoomed means sped or moved past fast.

clue.text: Moor that is covered in sheep …

indicators.note: covered in says the first piece is wrapped round the second

parts.note: a tup is a ram
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A stretch of moorland that is dotted with sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moor' looks like heathland but is the verb for securing a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To moor a boat is to tie it up at a jetty or buoy.

clue.text: … sheep circling about in pursuit of a drink

indicators.note: in pursuit of means coming after, so the word a comes first
circling says the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: a merino is a breed of sheep
CA, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, sheep wander around chasing a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 9-across's sheep for the surface only; 'in pursuit of' puts the sheep piece after A.
explanation.definitionFit: An Americano is a coffee drink of espresso topped up with hot water.

clue.text: Bird and small horse lying around in pool next to river

indicators.note: in says the piece goes inside the next one named

parts.note: a mere is a lake or pool

indicators.note: lying around suggests the small horse turned round, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a nag is a horse, usually an old one

explanation.surface: A bird and a little pony lounge about in a pond by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying around' makes GANS, the reversed small horse; 'next to' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The merganser is a fish-eating diving duck with a serrated bill.

clue.text: Singer's album downloads exceed low expectations at launch

indicators.note: at launch says take the starting letter of each of the words

explanation.surface: A singer's new record does better in downloads than people expected.
explanation.definitionFit: Adele is the British singer famous for albums such as 21 and 25.

clue.text: Comic routines consisting of extremely slapdash moments

indicators.note: extremely means taking the letters at the extremes, the first and last

parts.note: a tick is a moment, as in 'just a tick'

explanation.surface: A comedian's sets are full of sloppy moments.
explanation.definitionFit: A shtick is a comedian's familiar gimmick or routine.

clue.text: Carried on working unnoticed

indicators.note: working suggests letters being worked over and put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone kept at their job without anyone noticing.
explanation.definitionFit: Continued means went on or persisted, the same as carried on.

clue.text: Cope with basic accommodation, but not at first

indicators.note: not at first says the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a shack is a crude hut, very basic accommodation

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to put up with rough lodgings early on.
explanation.definitionFit: To hack it is informal for managing or coping with something.

clue.text: Spoilt, naughty child shown on TV

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
a programme is aired when it is broadcast

explanation.surface: A spoilt brat appears on a television show.
explanation.definitionFit: Impaired means damaged or weakened, as something spoilt is.

clue.text: Fancy bun scoffed and not licked!

indicators.note: fancy suggests the word dressed up in a different form, its letters rearranged

parts.note: to scoff food is to eat it greedily

explanation.surface: A fancy bun was gobbled down without anyone licking it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Licked' looks like tongue on icing; here it is slang for beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: To be licked is slang for being defeated, so someone never licked is undefeated.

clue.text: Politicians north of the border taking a break

indicators.note: taking means the first piece takes in, or holds, the next

parts.note: the SNP is the Scottish National Party; north of the border means in Scotland

explanation.surface: Scottish politicians go on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: The SNP is the Scottish National Party; 'north of the border' is the British way of saying Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: To snap is to break suddenly and cleanly.

clue.text: Sample survey given to people up front

indicators.note: up front says this letter is placed at the start of the other

parts.note: P is short for people
a review is a survey or general overview

explanation.surface: A trial questionnaire is handed out to the public in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: To preview something is to sample or try it before it is released.

clue.text: He's a rubbish worker and must get reassigned

indicators.note: reassigned suggests the letters being given new positions

explanation.surface: A refuse collector is told he must take a new round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish worker' tempts as an insult, but means someone who collects rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A dustman is the British word for a refuse collector, who works collecting household waste.

clue.text: Lots of information somewhat rejected by firm

indicators.note: rejected suggests being thrown back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a tad means somewhat, a little
set means firm, as a jelly sets

explanation.surface: A company turns down quite a bit of data.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somewhat' is A TAD, which 'rejected' turns to DATA.
explanation.definitionFit: A dataset is a collection of records, a large body of information.

clue.text: Some hash is handy for a pipe

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A little cannabis is useful to have for smoking.
explanation.definitionFit: Shisha is the flavoured tobacco smoked in a water pipe, so it is stuff meant for a pipe.

clue.text: Before I have left at the end, he's certain to cry

indicators.note: Before says these letters come ahead of the others
at the end says take the final letter of each of the two words

parts.note: I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A man is sure to weep before he departs at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the end' applies to both words of "he's certain", not to 'left', which just gives its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To snivel is to cry in a whining, sniffling way.

clue.text: Language of south India

indicators.note: of says the answer is made of letters taken from the words following

explanation.surface: Asking for a language spoken in the south of India.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a southern language such as Tamil; in fact the answer, mostly a northern language, sits in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindi is one of the official languages of India.

clue.text: Moderate old gallery contains space for all to see

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: contains says the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: the Tate is the famous London art gallery
an en is a printer's space
U is the British film certificate meaning universal, suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned art gallery has room for everyone to view its works.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a London art gallery; U is the British film certificate for all ages.
explanation.definitionFit: To extenuate an offence is to lessen or tone down its seriousness.

clue.text: Explosive start sees the two leaders switching places

indicators.note: the two leaders switching places means the opening pair of letters swap round

parts.note: an intro, short for introduction, is a start

explanation.surface: A dramatic opening where two front-runners swap positions.
explanation.walkthrough: INTRO with I and N swapped gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitro, short for nitroglycerine, is a powerful explosive.

clue.text: A serious drunk devouring five sausage rolls?

indicators.note: devouring says the first piece takes the second inside it
drunk suggests letters staggering into a new order

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A very drunk person wolfs down a handful of snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' rearranges A SERIOUS, which 'devouring' takes in V. The question mark marks sausage rolls as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Sausage rolls are a kind of savoury snack, so they illustrate the plural category.

clue.text: Jack returned to deck of cards

parts.note: a jack tar, or tar, is a sailor

indicators.note: returned says the little word comes back, so it is written the other way round

explanation.surface: A jack goes back into a pack of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a playing card but is a sailor, a TAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarot is a pack of cards used for fortune-telling.

clue.text: Everybody said it's a boring thing

indicators.note: said signals that the word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: all means everybody, as in all were there

explanation.surface: Everyone agrees something is tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' looks like dull but means making holes.
explanation.definitionFit: An awl is a pointed tool used for piercing holes in leather or wood.

clue.text: Oppressed, unhappy staff hiding in back of secret lair

parts.note: down means low in spirits

indicators.note: hiding in says the piece is concealed inside the others
back of says take the final letter of the word

parts.note: a den is an animal's lair
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: Miserable employees are tucked away at the rear of a secret hideout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back of' applies only to 'secret'; the lair follows it, and the staff hides between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Downtrodden people are oppressed, kept down by those with power.
